absent: Definitions and ordering guarantees of acquisition and release guards and timestamp and bad ring helpers.
Full layouts of virtual queue and split and packed ring and descriptor state and extra structures.
Implementations of split used position and identifier readers and split unmap and map helpers and unmap predicates.
Semantics of ordered mode detection and indirect selection and weak barrier and event capability flags.
Packed kick preparation and poll and completion and callback and detach and reset and resize paths beyond the truncated tail of this lane.

findings.text: Split indirect reclaim is idempotent on empty slots and otherwise validates the stored table before freeing it. It requires a nonzero byte length that divides evenly by one descriptor and requires the indirect marker, releases each secondary entry through the mapping layer only when that layer is enabled, frees the secondary storage, and clears the cached pointer.

Split chain reclaim clears the stored driver token, follows the chaining marker across first level entries while crediting one free slot per visited entry including the tail, then either frees any secondary table or returns the stored context. The unordered form additionally splices the whole reclaimed chain in front of the prior free head by linking its tail forward.

Split completion checks compare a snapshot of the consumed position with the device published used position. The primitive reports inequality, the common helper supplies the queue consumed value, and the ordered helper also reports work whenever a cached batch entry is still awaiting delivery.

Unordered split retrieval declines when the queue is marked broken or no completion is advertised, orders visibility of the used slot with the selected read barrier, indexes the used ring by masking with ring size, rejects an out of range identifier and a slot lacking a live head token, detaches the selected chain, advances the consumed position by one, conditionally publishes the new event position with an ordered store unless suppression is active, and invalidates the last add timestamp.

Ordered split retrieval delivers heads in submission order using a one entry cache whose empty value is UINT_MAX. The cache is filled once from the used ring after a barrier, length comes from the cache on identifier match and otherwise from accumulated input length, liveness is validated, the head is detached without reordering the free list, and both submission and consumed positions advance by the number of slots just freed before the same conditional event publication.

Split callback control keeps a shadow suppression marker. Disabling sets the marker and, unless an event already fired, writes zero to the used event when indexed events are active and otherwise publishes shadow flags to available flags. Enabling clears the marker and publishes the current consumed position as the event, while the delayed form publishes three quarters of the outstanding count ahead and reports whether pending completions already exceed that threshold.

Unused buffer reclamation scans descriptor states in index order for the first live driver token, reclaims it with the ordered or unordered helper matching queue mode, withdraws one from the shadow available count and republishes the available index, and treats a full scan with no live token as proof that free count equals ring size.

Split reset clears available and used flags and indices and clears both event slots that immediately follow the rings, then invokes the generic queue initializer and the split ring initializer to restore an empty queue.

Split resize allocates a replacement ring of the requested size together with fresh state and extra tables. Success releases the old ring and installs and initializes the new one, while any allocation failure leaves the old queue in reset state and reports memory exhaustion without installing partial state.
Split used event storage is the available ring array element at index equal to ring size, immediately following the last descriptor index.

Split wire markers comprise a chaining flag named VRING_DESC_F_NEXT plus a secondary table flag named VRING_DESC_F_INDIRECT plus an interrupt suppression bit named VRING_AVAIL_F_NO_INTERRUPT, where a secondary table length must be positive and an exact multiple of one descriptor.

Packed wire markers comprise an available phase bit named VRING_PACKED_DESC_F_AVAIL plus a used phase bit named VRING_PACKED_DESC_F_USED plus a device writable bit named VRING_DESC_F_WRITE plus the chaining and indirect flags, with a wrap counter bit named VRING_PACKED_EVENT_F_WRAP_CTR carried in event indices and masked to obtain the bare index.

All queue inspection and mutation here pairs an acquire marker named START_USE with a matching release marker named END_USE on every exit path, including broken queue, empty queue, and allocation or mapping failure, so free counts and indices and descriptor visibility are never observed mid update.

Indirect mapping state is stored as an extra array placed immediately after its descriptor array in a single allocation, with entry count derived from byte length divided by descriptor size, where each extra holds address and length and direction information consulted only when the mapping layer is active.

Packed queue bookkeeping maintains a next available position with phase flags and a wrap counter, a free head with free and added counts, and per identifier records holding descriptor count and driver token and secondary or context pointer and chain tail and total input length.

Packed indirect submission describes a whole scatter list with one ring slot. It maps each segment for device read or write according to output versus input membership, records address and length and writability in the secondary table, maps that table itself, publishes the head with the indirect marker only after a write barrier, advances the available position with phase inversion on wrap, and records token and table and input total, unwinding mappings and freeing the table on failure.

Unordered packed direct submission first tries the indirect path and continues directly only after memory pressure, requires enough free slots, maps segments in free list order marking every entry except the last as chained and input entries as writable, withholds head visibility until later entries are visible behind a write barrier, then advances availability and free bookkeeping, restoring prior phase and unpublishing exposed followers and unmapping on mapping failure.

Ordered packed direct submission lays segments sequentially from the next available position with identifier equal to head position, accumulates writable length into an input total, inverts phase flags and wrap counter across ring wrap, publishes the head last behind a write barrier, updates free and added counts, and on failure restores the saved phase and wrap state while unpublishing and unmapping the partial chain.

Completions become readable only after the selected read barrier, descriptor chains become available head last behind a write barrier, and event index publication uses an ordered store. A weak barrier mode selects virtualization primitives while the strong mode selects direct memory access read barrier and write plus full barrier sequences.

Malformed rings and misuse are treated as fatal rather than skipped. Unexpected secondary length or missing indirect marker, out of range completion identifier, completion without a live head token, absent driver token, and context combined with indirect mode trigger bug or bad ring handling.

Broken queues reject submission, exhausted free space reports shortage without mutation, and mapping or allocation failures unwind partial work. Indirect exhaustion falls back to direct only for memory pressure named ENOMEM, shortage reports ENOSPC, device or mapping failure reports EIO, and resize failure restores reset state with ENOMEM.

These fragments supply split completion and reclamation through unordered and ordered retrieval plus unused detachment and callback suppression and rearming, together with split reset and resize and packed submission in indirect and unordered direct and ordered direct forms, all operating on an internal virtual queue object.
Split queue operations are forward declared in this unit, so the operation table contents and dispatch wiring lie outside these fragments.
